ch22.d.preset: Starting arrangement of the charges (drag to move; the tray at the lower left adds and removes)
ch22.d.view: Draw the field as grid arrows, field lines, or both
ch22.d.test: Test charge $q_0$ and the Coulomb forces on it (each charge's force and the net force)
ch22.goal.field: Electric field: the force per unit charge on a test charge at each point, $\vec E = \vec F / q_0$
ch22.goal.super: Superposition: the field of several charges is the vector sum of the fields of each charge
ch22.obs.drag: Drag a charge and the whole field updates at once. Field lines leave positive charges and end on negative ones
ch22.obs.tray: Tray at the lower left: drag a charge out to add it, drop it back to remove it ($+1$, $+2$, $-1$, $-2$ nC)
ch22.obs.dipole: Dipole: the field is strongest between the charges and falls off quickly farther away
ch22.obs.like: Like pair: a point of zero field midway between the charges; the field lines push each other apart
ch22.obs.plates: Parallel plates: nearly uniform field between the plates, weak field outside
ch22.obs.test: Test charge: the vector sum of the Coulomb forces of the charges (thin arrows) is the net force $\vec F$ (thick arrow), of size $F = q_0 E$
ch22.as.units: Charges in nC, lengths in m
ch22.as.test: Test charge $q_0 = +1$ nC. Source charges are held fixed (the force of the test charge on them is ignored)
ch22.as.log: Grid arrow length is a log scale of the field strength (over three decades); the direction is exact
ch22.as.force: Force arrows share a linear scale set by the largest force. With 7 or more charges only the net force is drawn
ch22.as.plates: Each plate is approximated by 8 point charges. The number of field lines is proportional to the charge (10 per nC)
